open Real

/-- `RayFromThrough V P B C` is the set of points of the ray in the affine space `P` (over `V`)
starting at `B` and passing through `C`. It is parametrized as
`{ t • (C -ᵥ B) +ᵥ B | t ≥ 0 }`. -/
def RayFromThrough (V P : Type*)
  [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℝ V] [AddTorsor V P]
  (B C : P) : Set P :=
  { X | ∃ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t ∧ X = t • (C -ᵥ B) +ᵥ B }


-- >> Helper Definitions and Theorems
-- [Open a namespace for ray from B through C to define helper functions and theorems.]
-- [This separation is crucial to avoid namespace errors.]
namespace RayFromThrough

variable {V P : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℝ V] [AddTorsor V P]
variable {B C : P}

/-- The direction vector of the ray from `B` through `C`. -/
def dir (B C : P) : V := C -ᵥ B

/-- The parametrization of the ray from `B` through `C` by a real parameter `t`. -/
def param (B C : P) (t : ℝ) : P := t • (C -ᵥ B) +ᵥ B

/-- Characterization of membership in the ray as an existential over the nonnegative parameter. -/
theorem mem_iff {X : P} :
    X ∈ RayFromThrough V P B C ↔ ∃ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t ∧ X = t • (C -ᵥ B) +ᵥ B :=
  Iff.rfl

/-- Any point obtained by a nonnegative parameter lies on the ray. -/
theorem mem_of_nonneg_param {t : ℝ} (ht : 0 ≤ t) :
    param B C t ∈ RayFromThrough V P B C :=
  ⟨t, ht, rfl⟩

/-- The base point `B` lies on the ray (corresponding to parameter `t = 0`). -/
theorem base_mem : B ∈ RayFromThrough V P B C := by
  refine ⟨0, le_rfl, ?_⟩
  simpa [param, zero_smul, zero_vadd]

/-- The point `C` lies on the ray (corresponding to parameter `t = 1`). -/
theorem through_mem : C ∈ RayFromThrough V P B C := by
  refine ⟨1, zero_le_one, ?_⟩
  simpa [param, one_smul] using (vsub_vadd C B).symm

/-- If `X` lies on the ray, then `X` belongs to the affine span of `{B, C}`. -/
theorem subset_affineSpan_pair :
    RayFromThrough V P B C ⊆ affineSpan ℝ ({B, C} : Set P) := by
  intro X hX
  rcases hX with ⟨t, ht, rfl⟩
  set s := affineSpan ℝ ({B, C} : Set P)
  have hsubset : ({B, C} : Set P) ⊆ s := by
    simpa [s] using subset_affineSpan ℝ ({B, C} : Set P)
  have hB : B ∈ s := hsubset (by simp)
  have hC : C ∈ s := hsubset (by simp)
  have hdir_vec : C -ᵥ B ∈ s.direction := s.vsub_mem_direction hC hB
  have hdir_smul : t • (C -ᵥ B) ∈ s.direction := s.direction.smul_mem t hdir_vec
  exact s.vadd_mem_of_mem_direction hdir_smul hB

end RayFromThrough

/-- A simple specification of a circular sector by its radius and arc length.
The sector's (signed) area is defined to be `1/2 * radius * arcLength`. -/
structure SectorAreaHalfRadiusTimesArcLength where
  radius : ℝ
  arcLength : ℝ


-- >> Helper Definitions and Theorems
-- [Open a namespace for sector area = 1/2 r × arc length to define helper functions and theorems.]
-- [This separation is crucial to avoid namespace errors.]
namespace SectorAreaHalfRadiusTimesArcLength

noncomputable section

/-- The area of the circular sector: `1/2 * radius * arcLength`. -/
def area (S : SectorAreaHalfRadiusTimesArcLength) : ℝ :=
  (1 / 2) * S.radius * S.arcLength

/-- Construct a sector by specifying its radius and central angle (in radians).
The arc length is taken to be `radius * angle`. -/
def ofAngle (r θ : ℝ) : SectorAreaHalfRadiusTimesArcLength :=
  { radius := r
    arcLength := r * θ }

/-- The fundamental relation for a circular sector: area equals `1/2 * r * L`. -/
@[simp] theorem area_eq_half_mul_radius_mul_arcLength
    (S : SectorAreaHalfRadiusTimesArcLength) :
    S.area = (1 / 2) * S.radius * S.arcLength := rfl

/-- If the arc length equals `radius * angle` (angle in radians), then
`area = (1/2) * radius^2 * angle`. -/
theorem area_of_angle
    (S : SectorAreaHalfRadiusTimesArcLength) {θ : ℝ}
    (hL : S.arcLength = S.radius * θ) :
    S.area = (1 / 2) * S.radius ^ 2 * θ := by
  simp [area, hL, pow_two, mul_comm, mul_left_comm, mul_assoc]

/-- Special case of the angle formula for the sector built from an angle. -/
@[simp] theorem area_ofAngle (r θ : ℝ) :
    (ofAngle r θ).area = (1 / 2) * r ^ 2 * θ := by
  simp [area, ofAngle, pow_two, mul_comm, mul_left_comm, mul_assoc]

/-- A derived angle (in radians) from the arc length, defined as `arcLength / radius`
when `radius ≠ 0`, and `0` otherwise. -/
def angleFromArc (S : SectorAreaHalfRadiusTimesArcLength) : ℝ :=
  if S.radius = 0 then 0 else S.arcLength / S.radius

/-- When `radius ≠ 0`, the derived angle satisfies `arcLength = radius * angle`. -/
theorem arcLength_eq_radius_mul_angleFromArc
    (S : SectorAreaHalfRadiusTimesArcLength) (hR : S.radius ≠ 0) :
    S.arcLength = S.radius * S.angleFromArc := by
  unfold angleFromArc
  have hEq : S.arcLength = S.radius * (S.arcLength / S.radius) := by
    calc
      S.arcLength = S.arcLength * 1 := by simpa
      _ = S.arcLength * (S.radius / S.radius) := by simp [div_self hR]
      _ = S.radius * (S.arcLength / S.radius) := by
        simp [div_eq_mul_inv, mul_comm, mul_left_comm, mul_assoc]
  simpa [hR] using hEq

/-- When `radius ≠ 0`, the area can be written as `(1/2) * radius^2 * angleFromArc`. -/
theorem area_eq_half_mul_radius_sq_mul_angleFromArc
    (S : SectorAreaHalfRadiusTimesArcLength) (hR : S.radius ≠ 0) :
    S.area = (1 / 2) * S.radius ^ 2 * S.angleFromArc := by
  have hL : S.arcLength = S.radius * S.angleFromArc :=
    arcLength_eq_radius_mul_angleFromArc S hR
  simpa [area, hL, pow_two, mul_comm, mul_left_comm, mul_assoc]

/-- If `radius ≥ 0` and `arcLength ≥ 0`, then the sector area is nonnegative. -/
theorem area_nonneg
    (S : SectorAreaHalfRadiusTimesArcLength)
    (hR : 0 ≤ S.radius) (hL : 0 ≤ S.arcLength) :
    0 ≤ S.area := by
  have h12 : 0 ≤ (1 / 2 : ℝ) := one_half_pos.le
  have hmul : 0 ≤ ((1 / 2 : ℝ) * S.radius) := mul_nonneg h12 hR
  simpa [area, mul_assoc] using mul_nonneg hmul hL

end

end SectorAreaHalfRadiusTimesArcLength

given by its base radius `radius` and slant height `slantHeight`.
The (signed) lateral area is defined to be `π * radius * slantHeight`. -/
structure ConeLateralAreaPiRadiusSlantHeight where
  radius : ℝ
  slantHeight : ℝ

-- [Open a namespace for lateral area = π r l to define helper functions and theorems.]
-- [This separation is crucial to avoid namespace errors.]
namespace ConeLateralAreaPiRadiusSlantHeight

noncomputable section

/-- The lateral area of the cone: `π * radius * slantHeight`. -/
def lateralArea (C : ConeLateralAreaPiRadiusSlantHeight) : ℝ :=
  Real.pi * C.radius * C.slantHeight

/-- The circular base circumference, `2 * π * radius`. -/
def baseCircumference (C : ConeLateralAreaPiRadiusSlantHeight) : ℝ :=
  2 * Real.pi * C.radius

/-- View the cone's lateral surface as a circular sector whose radius is the slant height
and whose arc length is the base circumference `2 * π * radius`. -/
def asSector (C : ConeLateralAreaPiRadiusSlantHeight) : SectorAreaHalfRadiusTimesArcLength :=
  { radius := C.slantHeight
    arcLength := 2 * Real.pi * C.radius }

/-- The arc length of the associated sector is exactly the base circumference. -/
@[simp] theorem asSector_arcLength (C : ConeLateralAreaPiRadiusSlantHeight) :
    (C.asSector).arcLength = C.baseCircumference := rfl

/-- By the sector area formula `area = (1/2) * r * L`, the cone's lateral area
equals `π * radius * slantHeight`. -/
@[simp] theorem asSector_area_eq_lateralArea (C : ConeLateralAreaPiRadiusSlantHeight) :
    (C.asSector).area = C.lateralArea := by
  simp [asSector, lateralArea, SectorAreaHalfRadiusTimesArcLength.area,
        mul_comm, mul_left_comm, mul_assoc, one_div]

/-- A convenience simp lemma for the lateral area expression. -/
@[simp] theorem lateralArea_eq_pi_mul_radius_mul_slantHeight
    (C : ConeLateralAreaPiRadiusSlantHeight) :
    C.lateralArea = Real.pi * C.radius * C.slantHeight := rfl

/-- If `radius ≥ 0` and `slantHeight ≥ 0`, then the lateral area is nonnegative. -/
theorem lateralArea_nonneg
    (C : ConeLateralAreaPiRadiusSlantHeight)
    (hR : 0 ≤ C.radius) (hL : 0 ≤ C.slantHeight) :
    0 ≤ C.lateralArea := by
  have hπ : 0 ≤ Real.pi := Real.pi_pos.le
  have hmul : 0 ≤ Real.pi * C.radius := mul_nonneg hπ hR
  simpa [lateralArea, mul_assoc] using mul_nonneg hmul hL

/-- The cone built from explicit `radius` and `slantHeight`. -/
def ofParams (r l : ℝ) : ConeLateralAreaPiRadiusSlantHeight :=
  { radius := r, slantHeight := l }

/-- The lateral area of the cone built from parameters `r` and `l`. -/
@[simp] theorem lateralArea_ofParams (r l : ℝ) :
    (ofParams r l).lateralArea = Real.pi * r * l := rfl

/-- The associated sector for the cone built from parameters `r` and `l`. -/
@[simp] def asSector_ofParams (r l : ℝ) : SectorAreaHalfRadiusTimesArcLength :=
  (ofParams r l).asSector

/-- The sector area equals the cone's lateral area for parameters `r, l`. -/
@[simp] theorem asSector_ofParams_area (r l : ℝ) :
    (asSector_ofParams r l).area = Real.pi * r * l := by
  simpa using (asSector_area_eq_lateralArea (ofParams r l))

end

end ConeLateralAreaPiRadiusSlantHeight

/--
EuclideanPrism represents a prism in a real inner product space `V` formed by
translating a base polygon `base` by a fixed vector `shift`. The "top" face is
`EuclideanPolygon.translate base shift`, and the lateral faces consist of segments
joining each base vertex to its translated counterpart.
-/
structure EuclideanPrism (V : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℝ V] where
  base : EuclideanPolygon V
  shift : V


-- >> Helper Definitions and Theorems
-- [Open a namespace for Prism to define helper functions and theorems.]
-- [This separation is crucial to avoid namespace errors.]
namespace EuclideanPrism
noncomputable section

open EuclideanPolygon
open EuclideanPoint

variable {V : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℝ V]

/-- The top face of the prism is the translation of the base polygon by `shift`. -/
def topPolygon (P : EuclideanPrism V) : EuclideanPolygon V :=
  EuclideanPolygon.translate P.base P.shift

/-- The list of base vertices of the prism. -/
def baseVertices (P : EuclideanPrism V) : List (EuclideanPoint V) :=
  P.base.vertices

/-- The list of top vertices of the prism (each base vertex translated by `shift`). -/
def topVertices (P : EuclideanPrism V) : List (EuclideanPoint V) :=
  P.base.vertices.map (fun p => EuclideanPoint.translate p P.shift)

/-- The vertical edges of the prism: for each base vertex `p`, the segment `(p, p + shift)`. -/
def verticalEdges (P : EuclideanPrism V) :
    List ((EuclideanPoint V) × (EuclideanPoint V)) :=
  P.base.vertices.map (fun p => (p, EuclideanPoint.translate p P.shift))

/-- The displacement vectors along the vertical edges (each equals `shift`). -/
def verticalVecs (P : EuclideanPrism V) : List V :=
  (verticalEdges P).map (fun e => EuclideanPoint.vec e.fst e.snd)

/-- The distances along the vertical edges (each equals `‖shift‖`). -/
def verticalEdgeDistances (P : EuclideanPrism V) : List ℝ :=
  (verticalEdges P).map (fun e => EuclideanPoint.dist e.fst e.snd)

/-- All boundary edges of the prism: base edges, top edges, and vertical edges. -/
def boundaryEdges (P : EuclideanPrism V) :
    List ((EuclideanPoint V) × (EuclideanPoint V)) :=
  (EuclideanPolygon.edges P.base)
    ++ (EuclideanPolygon.edges (topPolygon P))
    ++ (verticalEdges P)

/-- The list of boundary edge lengths. -/
def boundaryLengths (P : EuclideanPrism V) : List ℝ :=
  (boundaryEdges P).map (fun e => EuclideanPoint.dist e.fst e.snd)

/-- The total boundary length (sum of all boundary edge lengths). -/
def boundaryLength (P : EuclideanPrism V) : ℝ :=
  (boundaryLengths P).foldl (fun acc x => acc + x) 0

/-- The Euclidean norm of the prism shift vector (the common vertical edge length). -/
def heightNorm (P : EuclideanPrism V) : ℝ :=
  ‖P.shift‖

/-- Translating the entire prism by a vector `v` translates both base and top faces. -/
def translate (P : EuclideanPrism V) (v : V) : EuclideanPrism V :=
  { base := EuclideanPolygon.translate P.base v
    shift := P.shift }

/-- The number of vertical edges equals the number of base vertices. -/
theorem verticalEdges_length (P : EuclideanPrism V) :
    (verticalEdges P).length = P.base.vertices.length := by
  simp [verticalEdges, List.length_map]

/-- The number of top vertices equals the number of base vertices. -/
theorem topVertices_length (P : EuclideanPrism V) :
    (topVertices P).length = P.base.vertices.length := by
  simp [topVertices, List.length_map]

/-- The number of boundary lengths equals the number of boundary edges. -/

    (boundaryLengths P).length = (boundaryEdges P).length := by
  simp [boundaryLengths]

/--
`TrapezoidBase` packages the data of a chosen base side `p–q` of a trapezoid in an affine space,
together with the opposite side `oppLeft–oppRight`, required to be parallel to the base.

The vectors `q -ᵥ p` and `oppRight -ᵥ oppLeft` witness the pair of parallel sides.
-/
structure TrapezoidBase (V P : Type*)
    [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℝ V] [AddTorsor V P] where
  p : P
  q : P
  base_ne : p ≠ q
  oppLeft : P
  oppRight : P

/-- The vector along the base side `p–q`. -/
def baseVec (tb : TrapezoidBase V P) : V :=
  tb.q -ᵥ tb.p

/-- The vector along the opposite side `oppLeft–oppRight`. -/
def oppositeVec (tb : TrapezoidBase V P) : V :=
  tb.oppRight -ᵥ tb.oppLeft

/-- The Euclidean length of the base side (the norm of its difference vector). -/
def baseLength (tb : TrapezoidBase V P) : ℝ :=
  ‖tb.baseVec‖

/-- The Euclidean length of the opposite side. -/
def oppositeLength (tb : TrapezoidBase V P) : ℝ :=
  ‖tb.oppositeVec‖

/-- The non-degeneracy of the base side implies its direction vector is nonzero. -/
theorem baseVec_ne_zero (tb : TrapezoidBase V P) : tb.baseVec ≠ 0 := by
  intro h
  have hEq : tb.q = tb.p := by
    simpa using (vsub_eq_zero_iff_eq).1 h
  exact tb.base_ne hEq.symm

/-- The non-degeneracy of the opposite side implies its direction vector is nonzero. -/
theorem oppositeVec_ne_zero (tb : TrapezoidBase V P) : tb.oppositeVec ≠ 0 := by
  intro h
  have hEq : tb.oppRight = tb.oppLeft := by
    simpa using (vsub_eq_zero_iff_eq).1 h
  exact tb.opposite_ne hEq.symm

/-- The base length is strictly positive. -/
theorem baseLength_pos (tb : TrapezoidBase V P) : 0 < tb.baseLength := by
  have hne : tb.baseVec ≠ 0 := tb.baseVec_ne_zero
  simpa [baseLength] using (norm_pos_iff.mpr hne)

/-- The opposite length is strictly positive. -/
theorem oppositeLength_pos (tb : TrapezoidBase V P) : 0 < tb.oppositeLength := by
  have hne : tb.oppositeVec ≠ 0 := tb.oppositeVec_ne_zero
  simpa [oppositeLength] using (norm_pos_iff.mpr hne)

/-- Restates the parallelism of the base and opposite sides as an explicit scalar relation. -/
theorem base_parallel_opposite (tb : TrapezoidBase V P) :
    VectorParallel tb.baseVec tb.oppositeVec :=
  tb.parallel

/-- There exists a real scalar `t` with `q -ᵥ p = t • (oppRight -ᵥ oppLeft)`. -/
theorem exists_scalar_rel (tb : TrapezoidBase V P) :
    ∃ t : ℝ, tb.baseVec = t • tb.oppositeVec := by
  simpa [baseVec, oppositeVec] using tb.parallel

/-- The base endpoints lie on the affine span generated by the base endpoints. -/
theorem base_endpoints_mem_affineSpan (tb : TrapezoidBase V P) :
    True := by

end TrapezoidBase

-- [Define the primary structure/class/def for unit consistency for area times length here.]
-- [Include its docstring and all necessary typeclass parameters.]
-- e.g.: structure {name_you_invent} (V P : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℝ V] ... where
--         ...
/--
AreaTimesLengthUnitConsistency encodes the dimensional consistency that:
- an area carries units of length squared,
- a length carries units of length,
- and their product carries units of length cubed.

It also provides a multiplicative model using `Units ℝ` to express that
the numerical values multiply in the expected way (cf. `Units.val_mul`),
while the unit exponents add (2 + 1 = 3), reflecting that volume has
units of length cubed (cf. intuition behind `EuclideanSpace.volume_ball_fin_three`).
-/
structure AreaTimesLengthUnitConsistency where
  areaU : Units ℝ
  lengthU : Units ℝ
  areaExponent : ℤ
  lengthExponent : ℤ
  area_is_two : areaExponent = 2
  length_is_one : lengthExponent = 1


-- >> Helper Definitions and Theorems
-- [Open a namespace for unit consistency for area times length to define helper functions and theorems.]
-- [This separation is crucial to avoid namespace errors.]
namespace AreaTimesLengthUnitConsistency

-- [Define all helper functions (like `nextVertices`, `edges`, `perimeter`)]
-- [and theorems (like `edges_length`, `perimeter_subset_affineSpan`)]
-- [that operate *on* `unit consistency for area times length` here.]

/-- The numerical area value underlying the unit-carrying area quantity. -/
def area (u : AreaTimesLengthUnitConsistency) : ℝ :=
  u.areaU.val

/-- The numerical length value underlying the unit-carrying length quantity. -/
def length (u : AreaTimesLengthUnitConsistency) : ℝ :=
  u.lengthU.val

/-- The unit-carrying product (interpreted as volume) as a unit in `ℝ`. -/
def volumeU (u : AreaTimesLengthUnitConsistency) : Units ℝ :=
  u.areaU * u.lengthU

/-- The numerical value of the unit-carrying product (interpreted as volume). -/
def volume (u : AreaTimesLengthUnitConsistency) : ℝ :=
  (volumeU u).val

/-- The unit exponent of the product is the sum of the exponents of area and length. -/
def volumeExponent (u : AreaTimesLengthUnitConsistency) : ℤ :=
  u.areaExponent + u.lengthExponent

/-- The numerical product agrees with multiplication of underlying values. -/
theorem volume_val (u : AreaTimesLengthUnitConsistency) :
    volume u = area u * length u := by
  unfold volume volumeU area length
  simpa using Units.val_mul u.areaU u.lengthU

/-- Dimensional consistency: area (length²) times length (length¹) gives volume (length³). -/
theorem volume_units_exponent_is_three (u : AreaTimesLengthUnitConsistency) :
    volumeExponent u = 3 := by
  unfold volumeExponent
  simpa [u.area_is_two, u.length_is_one]

/-- If both area and length are positive, then the product (volume) is positive. -/
theorem volume_pos_of_pos (u : AreaTimesLengthUnitConsistency)
    (ha : 0 < area u) (hl : 0 < length u) : 0 < volume u := by
  simpa [volume, area, length] using mul_pos ha hl

end AreaTimesLengthUnitConsistency

ordered list of vertices with length at least three. The boundary edges include the
closing edge from the last vertex back to the first.

structure EuclideanPolygon (V : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℝ V] where
  vertices : List (EuclideanPoint V)

variable {V : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℝ V]

/-- Build a polygon from a list and a length proof. -/
def ofList (L : List (EuclideanPoint V)) (h : 3 ≤ L.length) : EuclideanPolygon V :=
  { vertices := L
    length_ge_three := h }

/-- Extract the underlying list of vertices. -/
def toList (P : EuclideanPolygon V) : List (EuclideanPoint V) :=
  P.vertices

/-- The open edges of a polygon: consecutive vertex pairs without the closing edge. -/
def edgesOpen (P : EuclideanPolygon V) :
    List ((EuclideanPoint V) × (EuclideanPoint V)) :=
  P.vertices.zip (P.vertices.drop 1)

/-- The optional closing edge, from the last vertex back to the first. -/
def closingEdge? (P : EuclideanPolygon V) :
    Option ((EuclideanPoint V) × (EuclideanPoint V)) :=
  match P.vertices.head?, P.vertices.getLast? with
  | some h, some l => some (l, h)
  | _, _ => none

/-- All boundary edges of the polygon, including the closing edge when present. -/
def edges (P : EuclideanPolygon V) :
    List ((EuclideanPoint V) × (EuclideanPoint V)) :=
  match closingEdge? P with
  | some e => edgesOpen P ++ [e]
  | none => edgesOpen P

/-- Displacement vectors along the open edges. -/
def sideVecsOpen (P : EuclideanPolygon V) : List V :=
  (edgesOpen P).map (fun e => EuclideanPoint.vec e.fst e.snd)

/-- Displacement vectors along all edges (including the closing edge). -/
def sideVecs (P : EuclideanPolygon V) : List V :=
  (edges P).map (fun e => EuclideanPoint.vec e.fst e.snd)

/-- Side lengths (distances) along the open edges. -/
def sideLengthsOpen (P : EuclideanPolygon V) : List ℝ :=
  (edgesOpen P).map (fun e => EuclideanPoint.dist e.fst e.snd)

/-- Side lengths (distances) along all edges (including the closing edge). -/
def sideLengths (P : EuclideanPolygon V) : List ℝ :=
  (edges P).map (fun e => EuclideanPoint.dist e.fst e.snd)

/-- The open path length (sum of distances along open edges, omitting the closing edge). -/
def openPerimeter (P : EuclideanPolygon V) : ℝ :=
  (sideLengthsOpen P).foldl (fun acc x => acc + x) 0

/-- The polygon perimeter (sum of distances along all boundary edges). -/
def perimeter (P : EuclideanPolygon V) : ℝ :=
  (sideLengths P).foldl (fun acc x => acc + x) 0

/-- Translate the entire polygon by a fixed vector. -/
def translate (P : EuclideanPolygon V) (v : V) : EuclideanPolygon V :=
  { vertices := P.vertices.map (fun p => EuclideanPoint.translate p v)
    length_ge_three := by
      simpa [List.length_map] using P.length_ge_three }

/-- The list of raw coordinates of the polygon vertices. -/
def coords (P : EuclideanPolygon V) : List V :=
  P.vertices.map (fun p => p.coord)

/-- The polygon's vertices packaged as an `EuclideanPointList`. -/
def toPointList (P : EuclideanPolygon V) : EuclideanPointList V :=
  { pts := P.vertices }

/-- The number of open edges equals `length vertices - 1`. -/
theorem edgesOpen_length_eq_length_sub_one (P : EuclideanPolygon V) :
    (edgesOpen P).length = P.vertices.length - 1 := by
  sorry

/-- For a polygon (length ≥ 3), the number of boundary edges equals the number of vertices. -/
theorem edges_length_eq_vertices_length (P : EuclideanPolygon V) :
    (edges P).length = P.vertices.length := by
  sorry

/-- The number of side lengths equals the number of edges. -/
theorem sideLengths_length (P : EuclideanPolygon V) :
    (sideLengths P).length = (edges P).length := by
  sorry

/-- The open perimeter is nonnegative. -/
theorem openPerimeter_nonneg (P : EuclideanPolygon V) : 0 ≤ openPerimeter P := by
  sorry

/-- The perimeter is nonnegative. -/
theorem perimeter_nonneg (P : EuclideanPolygon V) : 0 ≤ perimeter P := by
  sorry

/-- Translating the polygon by a fixed vector preserves the perimeter. -/
theorem translate_preserves_perimeter (P : EuclideanPolygon V) (v : V) :
    perimeter (translate P v) = perimeter P := by
  sorry

/-- Membership in the coordinate list of the polygon vertices. -/
theorem mem_coords_iff {P : EuclideanPolygon V} {x : V} :
    x ∈ coords P ↔ ∃ p, p ∈ P.vertices ∧ p.coord = x := by
  sorry

/-- The coordinate list has the same length as the vertex list. -/
theorem coords_length (P : EuclideanPolygon V) :
    (coords P).length = P.vertices.length := by
  sorry

/-- Every vertex coordinate lies in the affine span of all vertex coordinates. -/
theorem vertices_subset_affineSpan_coords (P : EuclideanPolygon V) :
    ∀ p, p ∈ P.vertices → p.coord ∈ affineSpan ℝ {x | x ∈ coords P} := by
  sorry

/-- The sum of the displacement vectors around the closed polygon equals zero. -/
theorem sum_sideVecs_eq_zero (P : EuclideanPolygon V) :
    ((sideVecs P).foldl (fun acc v => acc + v) 0) = 0 := by
  sorry

/-- Coordinates after translation correspond to translating each coordinate by `v`. -/
theorem coords_translate (P : EuclideanPolygon V) (v : V) :
    coords (translate P v) = (coords P).map (fun x => x + v) := by
  sorry

end

open Real
open EuclideanGeometry
open FiniteDimensional

-- >> Main Definition
-- [You must first invent a single, valid, UpperCamelCase Lean identifier,based on SideCount.]
-- [Define the primary structure/class/def for SideCount here.]

--         ...

/-- SideCount represents a finite list of vertices for a polygon-like object.
The side count is intended to be the number of vertices, interpreting edges
as connections between consecutive vertices with the last connected back to the first. -/
structure SideCount (α : Type*) where
  vertices : List α
  nodup : vertices.Nodup

-- >> Helper Definitions and Theorems
-- [Open a namespace for SideCount to define helper functions and theorems.]
-- [This separation is crucial to avoid namespace errors.]
namespace SideCount

/-- The number of sides equals the number of vertices. -/
def sideCount {α : Type*} (S : SideCount α) : Nat :=
  S.vertices.length

/-- Non-cyclic consecutive pairs of a list: pairs `(xᵢ, xᵢ₊₁)` for all valid `i`. -/
def consecutivePairs {α : Type*} : List α → List (α × α)
  | [] => []
  | [_] => []
  | a :: b :: rest => (a, b) :: consecutivePairs (b :: rest)

/-- Auxiliary to build cyclic pairs after the initial pair `(first, curr)`:
continues through the tail and finally closes with `(last, first)`. -/
def cyclicPairsAux {α : Type*} (first curr : α) : List α → List (α × α)
  | [] => [(curr, first)]
  | b :: rest => (curr, b) :: cyclicPairsAux first b rest

/-- Cyclic consecutive pairs of a list, including the last-to-first edge when the list has at least two elements. -/
def cyclicPairs {α : Type*} (xs : List α) : List (α × α) :=
  match xs with
  | [] => []
  | [_] => []
  | a :: b :: rest => (a, b) :: cyclicPairsAux a b rest

/-- The edge list formed by connecting consecutive vertices cyclically. -/
def edges {α : Type*} (S : SideCount α) : List (α × α) :=
  cyclicPairs S.vertices

/-- Length of `cyclicPairsAux` is the tail length plus one (for the closing edge). -/
theorem cyclicPairsAux_length {α : Type*} (first curr : α) :
    ∀ rest : List α, (cyclicPairsAux first curr rest).length = rest.length + 1
  | [] => by simp [cyclicPairsAux]
  | b :: rest => by
      simp [cyclicPairsAux, cyclicPairsAux_length first b rest, Nat.add_comm, Nat.add_left_comm, Nat.add_assoc]

/-- The side count agrees with the length of the vertex list. -/
theorem sideCount_eq_length {α : Type*} (S : SideCount α) :
    sideCount S = S.vertices.length := rfl

/-- For lists with at least two elements, the cyclic pair list has the same length as the list. -/
theorem cyclicPairs_length_eq_length_of_two_or_more {α : Type*} :
    ∀ xs : List α, 2 ≤ xs.length → (cyclicPairs xs).length = xs.length
  | [], _ => by simp [cyclicPairs]
  | [a], h => by
      have h' : 2 ≤ 1 := by simpa using h
      exact False.elim ((Nat.not_succ_le_self 1) h')
  | a :: b :: rest, _ => by
      simp [cyclicPairs, cyclicPairsAux_length, List.length, Nat.add_comm, Nat.add_left_comm, Nat.add_assoc]

/-- For lists with fewer than two elements, there are no cyclic edges. -/
theorem cyclicPairs_length_zero_of_lt_two {α : Type*} :
    ∀ xs : List α, xs.length < 2 → (cyclicPairs xs).length = 0
  | [], _ => by simp [cyclicPairs]
  | [a], _ => by simp [cyclicPairs]
  | a :: b :: rest, h => by
      have h2 : 2 ≤ (a :: b :: rest).length := by
        simpa [List.length, Nat.add_comm, Nat.add_left_comm, Nat.add_assoc] using (Nat.le_add_right 2 rest.length)
      exact False.elim ((Nat.not_lt.mpr h2) h)

/-- If there are at least two vertices, the number of edges equals the side count. -/
theorem edges_length_eq_sideCount_of_two_or_more {α : Type*} (S : SideCount α)
    (h : 2 ≤ sideCount S) :
    (edges S).length = sideCount S := by
  simpa [edges, sideCount] using
    (cyclicPairs_length_eq_length_of_two_or_more S.vertices h)

/-- If there are fewer than two vertices, there are no edges. -/
theorem edges_length_zero_of_lt_two {α : Type*} (S : SideCount α)
    (h : sideCount S < 2) :
    (edges S).length = 0 := by
  simpa [edges, sideCount] using
    (cyclicPairs_length_zero_of_lt_two S.vertices h)

/-- The number of edges is at most the side count. -/
theorem edges_length_le_sideCount {α : Type*} (S : SideCount α) :
    (edges S).length ≤ sideCount S := by
  by_cases h : 2 ≤ sideCount S
  · exact le_of_eq (edges_length_eq_sideCount_of_two_or_more S h)
  ·
    have hlt : sideCount S < 2 := Nat.lt_of_not_ge h
    have hz : (edges S).length = 0 := edges_length_zero_of_lt_two S hlt
    simpa [hz] using (Nat.zero_le (sideCount S))

/-- The side count is nonnegative. -/
theorem sideCount_nonneg {α : Type*} (S : SideCount α) :
    0 ≤ sideCount S := by
  exact Nat.zero_le _

end SideCount

/--
EuclideanHexagon represents a cyclic hexagon in a real inner product space `V`
by an ordered list of exactly six vertices. The boundary edges include the
closing edge from the last vertex back to the first, forming a closed polygonal chain.
-/
structure EuclideanHexagon (V : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℝ V] where
  vertices : List (EuclideanPoint V)
  length_eq_six : vertices.length = 6


-- >> Helper Definitions and Theorems
-- [Open a namespace for Hexagon to define helper functions and theorems.]
-- [This separation is crucial to avoid namespace errors.]
namespace EuclideanHexagon
noncomputable section

variable {V : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℝ V]

/-- Build a hexagon from a list with a proof that its length is six. -/
def ofList (L : List (EuclideanPoint V)) (h : L.length = 6) : EuclideanHexagon V :=
  { vertices := L
    length_eq_six := h }

/-- Extract the underlying list of vertices. -/
def toList (H : EuclideanHexagon V) : List (EuclideanPoint V) :=
  H.vertices

/-- Translate the entire hexagon by a fixed vector. -/
def translate (H : EuclideanHexagon V) (v : V) : EuclideanHexagon V :=
  { vertices := H.vertices.map (fun p => EuclideanPoint.translate p v)
    length_eq_six := by
      simpa [List.length_map] using H.length_eq_six }

/-- The list of raw coordinates of the hexagon vertices. -/
def coords (H : EuclideanHexagon V) : List V :=
  H.vertices.map (fun p => p.coord)

/-- All boundary edges of the hexagon (cyclic consecutive pairs, including the closing edge). -/
def edges (H : EuclideanHexagon V) :
    List ((EuclideanPoint V) × (EuclideanPoint V)) :=
  SideCount.cyclicPairs H.vertices

/-- Displacement vectors along all edges. -/
def sideVecs (H : EuclideanHexagon V) : List V :=
  (edges H).map (fun e => EuclideanPoint.vec e.fst e.snd)

/-- Side lengths (distances) along all edges. -/
def sideLengths (H : EuclideanHexagon V) : List ℝ :=
  (edges H).map (fun e => EuclideanPoint.dist e.fst e.snd)

/-- The hexagon perimeter (sum of distances along all boundary edges). -/
def perimeter (H : EuclideanHexagon V) : ℝ :=
  (sideLengths H).foldl (fun acc x => acc + x) 0

/-- For a hexagon, the number of boundary edges equals six. -/
theorem edges_length_eq_six (H : EuclideanHexagon V) :
    (edges H).length = 6 := by
  have h2 : 2 ≤ H.vertices.length := by
    simpa [H.length_eq_six] using (by decide : 2 ≤ 6)
  simpa [edges, H.length_eq_six] using
    (SideCount.cyclicPairs_length_eq_length_of_two_or_more H.vertices h2)

/-- The number of side lengths equals the number of edges. -/
theorem sideLengths_length (H : EuclideanHexagon V) :
    (sideLengths H).length = (edges H).length := by
  simp [sideLengths, edges, List.length_map]

/-- The coordinate list has the same length as the vertex list. -/
theorem coords_length (H : EuclideanHexagon V) :
    (coords H).length = H.vertices.length := by
  simp [coords, List.length_map]

/-- Membership in the coordinate list of the hexagon vertices. -/
theorem mem_coords_iff {H : EuclideanHexagon V} {x : V} :
    x ∈ coords H ↔ ∃ p, p ∈ H.vertices ∧ p.coord = x := by
  simp [coords, List.mem_map]

/-- Auxiliary lemma: a fold of additions with nonnegative accumulator over a list
of nonnegative entries remains nonnegative. -/
lemma foldl_add_nonneg_of_all_nonneg_aux (xs : List ℝ) (acc : ℝ)
    (hacc : 0 ≤ acc) (hnonneg : ∀ x ∈ xs, 0 ≤ x) :
    0 ≤ xs.foldl (fun a x => a + x) acc := by
  induction xs generalizing acc with
  | nil =>
      simpa
  | cons x xs ih =>
      have hx : 0 ≤ x := hnonneg x (by simp)
      have hxs : ∀ y ∈ xs, 0 ≤ y := fun y hy => hnonneg y (by simp [hy])
      have hacc' : 0 ≤ acc + x := add_nonneg hacc hx
      simpa [List.foldl] using ih (acc + x) hacc' hxs

/-- Each side length (distance) is nonnegative. -/
lemma sideLengths_entry_nonneg {H : EuclideanHexagon V} {x : ℝ}
    (hx : x ∈ sideLengths H) : 0 ≤ x := by
  rcases List.mem_map.1 hx with ⟨e, he, rfl⟩
  simpa [EuclideanPoint.dist] using (norm_nonneg (e.snd.coord - e.fst.coord))

/-- The perimeter is nonnegative. -/
theorem perimeter_nonneg (H : EuclideanHexagon V) : 0 ≤ perimeter H := by
  have hentry : ∀ x ∈ sideLengths H, 0 ≤ x := by
    intro x hx; exact sideLengths_entry_nonneg (H := H) hx
  simpa [perimeter] using
    foldl_add_nonneg_of_all_nonneg_aux (sideLengths H) 0 (by exact le_rfl) hentry

end
end EuclideanHexagon

/--
IsRegularGraph G k is the predicate that a simple graph G is k-regular,
i.e., every vertex of G has degree exactly k.

def IsRegularGraph {α : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph α) (k : ℕ)
    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableRel G.Adj] : Prop :=
  ∀ v : α, G.degree v = k

    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableRel G.Adj]

  sorry

    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (h : IsRegularGraph G k) :
    2 * G.edgeFinset.card = Fintype.card α * k := by

theorem iff_forall_degree_eq
    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableRel G.Adj] :
    IsRegularGraph G k ↔ ∀ v : α, G.degree v = k := by
  sorry

/-- If a graph is k-regular and nonempty, then k equals the degree of any chosen vertex. -/
theorem const_degree_of_exists_vertex
    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (h : IsRegularGraph G k) (v : α) : k = G.degree v := by
